summary: Stipendium Hungaricum is a Hungarian government scholarship, managed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and coordinated by Tempus Public Foundation, for students from partner countries that have an education cooperation agreement with Hungary. It supports bachelor's, master's, one-tier master's and doctoral studies, mostly taught in English, and also a one-year Hungarian language preparatory course and postgraduate specialist courses. The scholarship exempts tuition and gives a monthly stipend, an accommodation contribution or dormitory place, and medical insurance. The details below come from the 2026/27 call; the 2027/28 call had not been published when checked.
eligibility_notes:
Country rule: you can apply only through the Sending Partner of your own citizenship, i.e. a country or territory that has a valid education cooperation agreement with Hungary. Your application counts only if the Sending Partner nominates you. Applicants with a citizenship different from the sending country are rejected. Applicants may apply only for the scholarship types and study fields set in the agreement between Hungary and their country.

Levels: bachelor's, master's, one-tier master's, non-degree (Hungarian language preparatory course) and postgraduate specialist courses are in one call; doctoral studies have a separate call. You may apply to one call or the other in the same round, not both.

Age (2026/27 call): applicants born after 31 August 2008 are not eligible, except applicants for dance programmes. The doctoral call text read does not repeat this rule.

Excluded (2026/27 call): Hungarian citizens including dual citizens; stateless persons, refugees, protected persons, asylum-seekers and people with long-term residence status; people who submit more than one application or use more than one account or Sending Partner; people who apply for a programme below the level of their current self-financed studies in Hungary; former scholarship holders who re-apply for the same or a lower level (they may apply for a higher level); people who still hold a scholarship at the application deadline and will not graduate by 31 August 2026, unless they withdraw it; people who postponed and did not withdraw; and people who accepted a scholarship in 2023/24, 2024/25 or 2025/26, never travelled and did not tell Tempus Public Foundation by 15 October. Scholarship status is also lost if a holder later becomes a Hungarian citizen or refugee.

Self-financed students already in Hungary at the same level may apply only if their Hungarian university recommends them and (for bachelor's and master's) their corrected cumulative average is above the programme average.

Education required: bachelor's applicants need a secondary school graduation certificate; master's applicants need a bachelor's degree certificate or equivalent; one-tier master's and preparatory course applicants need a secondary school certificate; doctoral applicants need a master's degree certificate or equivalent. Applicants in their last semester can upload the certificate later (see steps).

Language: you must meet the minimum language level of the host institution for the programme you choose; the exact level is shown on each programme in the online system. For Hungarian-taught programmes, applicants need at least intermediate (B2) Hungarian proof, otherwise they must take the one-year Hungarian preparatory course.

Students who start with the scholarship must also not hold another scholarship from the Hungarian central budget for studies in Hungary.
age_experience_notes: 2026/27 call: applicants born after 31 August 2008 (under 18 on 31 August 2026) are not eligible, except for dance programmes. No upper age limit and no work experience requirement are stated in the call text read.
funding_summary: Tuition is exempt. The monthly stipend is HUF 43,700 for non-degree, bachelor's, master's and one-tier master's students and HUF 140,000 (first four semesters) or HUF 180,000 (second four semesters) for doctoral students, paid for 12 months a year until the studies end. Accommodation is a free dormitory place (depending on capacity) or HUF 40,000 a month. Medical care and extra insurance of up to HUF 65,000 a year are included. The call says these amounts only contribute to living costs and do not cover everything; travel is not paid.
programmes_note: Study types in the 2026/27 call: bachelor's (BA/BSc, 2-4 years), master's (MA/MSc, 1-2 years), one-tier master's (5-6 years, for example general medicine, pharmacy, dentistry, architecture, law, veterinary surgery, forestry engineering), doctoral (8 semesters: 2+2 years), a one-year Hungarian language preparatory course and postgraduate specialist training (1-2 years). Each can also be partial (exchange) study of 1 or 2 semesters, if the agreement with the applicant's country allows it. About 900 foreign-language programmes are offered at bachelor's, master's and one-tier levels and about 170 doctoral programmes. You can choose up to two programmes in order of preference; the order, study language and study mode cannot be changed after the deadline. Which fields you can pick depends on the agreement with your country. The programme list and each programme's entry requirements are in the online application system, and a list of eligible full-degree and partial programmes was published as spreadsheets with the call.
institutions_note: The 2026/27 call states that 30 Hungarian higher education institutions take part at bachelor's, master's and one-tier level and 23 at doctoral level. The study finder page lists 33 entries in its university menu with their coordinators (for example Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Eotvos Lorand University, Semmelweis University, University of Debrecen, University of Szeged, University of Pecs, Corvinus University of Budapest, Liszt Ferenc Academy of Music, Hungarian Dance University, University of Veterinary Medicine). You do not apply to universities directly: Tempus Public Foundation forwards the documents of nominated applicants to the host institutions you chose, which hold the entrance examinations. Allocation between hosts depends on the agreement with your country, programme capacity, your order of preference, exam results and the Sending Partner ranking.

summary.detail: Doctoral degree, 8 semesters in two phases of 4 semesters; a complex exam at the end of the first phase decides whether the student continues. Monthly stipend HUF 140,000 in the first phase and HUF 180,000 in the second. About 170 programmes at 23 institutions in 2026/27. Needs a master's degree certificate or equivalent, a research plan, a recommendation letter and a supervisor at the host university (a supervisor statement where the doctoral school asks for it). Partial doctoral study of 1 or 2 semesters is also possible. Separate call for applications.

Non-degree programmes: (1) a one-year Hungarian language preparatory course, only for applicants who then continue in a Hungarian-taught degree programme, who apply for the course directly and not for the later degree; (2) postgraduate specialist training courses, 1-2 years (or 1-2 semesters partial), giving a certificate after a bachelor's or master's degree. Preparatory courses are not available for specialist training. For English-taught degrees in engineering, music and dance, or computer science and IT, the host institution may decide to admit a candidate first to a foundation semester or year; you cannot apply for this directly. Monthly stipend HUF 43,700.

benefits.conditions: For the study period of the scholarship.

benefits.limit_text: HUF 43,700 per month (non-degree, bachelor's, master's, one-tier master's); HUF 140,000 per month in the first doctoral phase and HUF 180,000 in the second phase
benefits.conditions: Paid 12 months a year until studies end. It is a contribution to living costs, not the whole cost. Full-degree bachelor's and master's holders must attend the Hungarian as a foreign language course in year one and pass the exam after the second semester (not required for Hungarian-taught programmes); without attending, no stipend; if they attend but fail, the stipend falls to HUF 30,000 a month. Allowances are not paid during an extension period.

benefits.limit_text: Free dormitory place (depending on institutional capacity) or HUF 40,000 per month
benefits.conditions: The HUF 40,000 is a contribution to rent for students who do not use a dormitory; in big cities, especially the capital, it will not cover the whole rent. Applies for the whole scholarship period.

benefits.limit_text: Health care under Hungarian law plus supplementary medical insurance up to HUF 65,000 per year per person
benefits.conditions: Health care is provided if the agreement with the sending country allows it. Medical examinations on arrival are free for holders.

benefits.limit_text: No money is provided for travel costs
benefits.conditions: Holders organise and pay their own travel to Hungary.

benefits.limit_text: Holders are exempt from fees related to admission to Hungary
benefits.conditions: Under current rules this covers admission-related fees. The scholarship does not guarantee a visa. No visa help, allowance or administrative services are given to family members or accompanying persons.
The call advises not to pay agencies.

requirements.text: Online application form, filled in English in the Tempus Public Foundation online system. It must be submitted, not only saved. Uploaded files can be at most 4 MB each.
A recent photo taken not more than 2 years before submission.

Motivation letter of at least 1 page, typed in Times New Roman size 12, written in the language of the chosen programme or in Hungarian. Applicants for partial studies state the length in months and the start month (September or February).

Scanned copy of the original proof of language proficiency at or above the host institution's minimum level, with a translation if it is not in the language of the programme or Hungarian. If your previous studies were in the same language, a document proving this can be uploaded instead.

School certificate: secondary school graduation certificate or equivalent for bachelor's, one-tier master's and the preparatory course; bachelor's degree certificate or equivalent for master's; master's degree certificate or equivalent for doctoral. Scanned original plus translation if not in the programme language or Hungarian. Partial studies: a certificate of student status from your current university, showing the status will last during the partial studies, where studies are part of your home degree or the host asks for it.
Copy of the transcript of records for all semesters or school years of your previous studies (highest level attended), plus translation if not in the programme language or Hungarian.

Scanned data page of your passport (page with personal data and photo). If you have no passport yet, upload your national ID card with a signed declaration that a valid passport will be uploaded by 1 August (the apply page gives this rule).

Acceptance of the Statement for Application, which you accept in the online system after registering. Do not upload a scanned signed copy. You must also accept the Privacy Notice and data consents to submit.
Research plan: at least 2 pages in Times New Roman size 12, written in the language of the programme; it must list the resources used and is checked for plagiarism.
Signed letter of recommendation from a former or current academic tutor or supervisor who holds a scientific degree and knows your work, written in the language of the programme or in Hungarian.

Statement of the supervisor at the host institution agreeing to supervise you. If you cannot upload it by the deadline, upload a declaration by the deadline and the statement by 15 March 2026. Two programmes that need it require two statements from two professors.
requirements.conditional_rule: Doctoral applicants, only where the doctoral school requires it

requirements.text: Portfolio of works of art (with creation dates) in the Media Files section, in the type and number the host institution sets; if over 4 MB, upload a document with download links.
requirements.conditional_rule: Applicants for arts and music programmes (arts only in the doctoral call)

requirements.text: Recommendation letter from the Hungarian host university, uploaded by 15 March 2026, plus (bachelor's and master's) a corrected cumulative average above the programme average.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only self-financed students already studying in Hungary at the same level

requirements.text: Medical certificate of satisfactory health on the official template, signed by a physician and issued not earlier than 1 November 2025 (2026/27 call). Do not upload it; bring it to Hungary for the compulsory medical examination. Not needed from Students at Risk applicants.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only applicants who win a scholarship

requirements.text: Missing documents: if a school certificate, degree certificate, language certificate or passport is not available by the deadline, upload a signed declaration by the deadline and the document by 1 August 2026 at the latest. Only final-semester students and applicants waiting for language results or a new passport qualify. No form is provided; no declaration or no later upload means rejection.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only where the document cannot be obtained by the deadline

application_steps.title: Read the call and check your country's agreement
application_steps.detail: Read the call for your level and check that your country has an education agreement with Hungary and which scholarship types and fields it covers. Choose up to two programmes in order of preference, at the same or different host institutions; the order, language and study mode are fixed after the deadline. Do not pay agencies and do not apply directly to universities.

application_steps.title: Contact your Sending Partner and follow its rules
application_steps.detail: Every application must also go to the responsible authority of your Sending Partner, which sets its own deadlines and may ask for hard copies. Contact it early. Some partners require no extra materials.

application_steps.title: Register and submit the online application
application_steps.detail: Register in the Tempus Public Foundation online system with an email you read often, upload all documents, accept the Statement for Application and data consents, and click submit before the deadline (15 January 2026, 2 p.m. CET in the 2026/27 round). One application per year, no changes to programmes after the deadline, and you can withdraw at any stage but not undo it.

application_steps.title: Technical check by Tempus Public Foundation
application_steps.detail: Submitted applications are checked for age, citizenship, earlier scholarships, whether the scholarship type and programme are open to your country, uploaded documents and the accepted statement. Failing any of these rejects the application automatically. Eligible applications go to your Sending Partner.

application_steps.title: Nomination by the Sending Partner
application_steps.detail: The Sending Partner ranks the applications and sends a nomination list with a reserve list to Tempus Public Foundation by the end of February (28 February 2026 in the 2026/27 round). Only nominated applicants continue. Winners of first, second or third place at the National Scientific Student Conference are nominated automatically.

application_steps.title: Entrance examination at the host institution
application_steps.detail: Hosts check documents and entry requirements, then examine each applicant in up to two rounds (first-choice programmes expected 18 March to 30 April 2026, second choices to 20 May 2026). Applicants are scored out of 100 points; the minimum is 56 points. Medical programme applicants should expect no consideration if the programme is only a second choice. Language tests apply for Hungarian-taught programmes.

application_steps.title: Allocation and results
application_steps.detail: Tempus Public Foundation allocates places using the agreement with your country, programme capacity, your preference order, exam points and the Sending Partner ranking; STEM+ fields get priority. You get one result email, around the end of June in 2026, with one of four statuses: approved, conditionally approved, pending or rejected. A pass in the exam is not itself a scholarship.

application_steps.title: Accept the scholarship in the online system
application_steps.detail: Accept the scholarship and agree to the Operational Regulations within the deadline in the notification email (usually one week, sometimes shorter) and no later than 1 August 2026 in the last round. Conditionally approved holders must also upload missing documents by that date. Not accepting counts as withdrawal.

application_steps.title: Apply for a visa and travel to Hungary
application_steps.detail: Start the visa application at once through the consulate; officially a visa can take up to 30 days and holders do not pay admission-related fees. Tell the host institution's coordinator your arrival date 30 days before, and not less than 15 days before. Arrive and register by 30 September 2026 or the host's date; late holders who do not withdraw by 15 October are excluded.

application_steps.title: Medical check, scholarship contract and enrolment
application_steps.detail: Bring the signed medical certificate for the free medical examination at the university. Sign the scholarship contract with the host institution, enrol in the semester you were admitted to, and arrange stipend and housing payments with the institutional coordinator.

application_steps.title: Keep the scholarship during your studies
application_steps.detail: Complete at least 18 credits on average over the last two active semesters (36 in total), usually 30 per semester. Live habitually in Hungary: absences over 30 days can cost allowances, and over 10 working days must be reported. During term you may work up to 30 hours a week; outside term, full time for up to 90 days a year. Another study-abroad scholarship for more than 30 days ends the award. Changing institution or programme is allowed once per level within a year of starting; extensions of up to two semesters exist for full-time bachelor's and master's students only, without allowances.
